headline: Thousands mock Trump's midterm setback at Tehran rally
description: Hours after US voters stripped President Donald Trump’s Republicans of control of Congress, partly over the Iran...
article_text:
Hours after US voters stripped President Donald Trump’s Republicans of control of Congress, partly over the Iran war, thousands gathered outside the former US embassy in Tehran for an annual anti-American rally, AFP reports.

Chants of “Death to America” and “Death to Israel” echoed through central Tehran as demonstrators waved Iranian flags and carried banners denouncing Washington and Israel.

“America has been tormenting us for years, but it has not been able to do anything to Iran,” said Mahmoudkhani, 40, who attended the rally marking the 1979 seizure of the embassy and the hostage crisis that followed.

One banner depicted Trump as a blood-stained bulldog on a leash held by a devil-like figure resembling Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Others called for revenge for martyred supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, killed by the US-Israeli strikes that sparked the regional war in late February.

The rally came a day after Trump’s blistering US midterm bashing, widely viewed as a referendum on his turbulent second term, with frustration over living costs, a rollercoaster of tariffs and the conflict with Iran playing a major role.

headline: After US midterm loss, Vice President JD Vance backs 'diplomatic solution' to Iran war
description: In his post on X, JD Vance also backed “political advice” given by TV personality Rachel Campos Duffy who he said...
article_text:
In his post on X, JD Vance also backed “political advice” given by TV personality Rachel Campos Duffy who he said called for a “diplomatic resolution” to the Iran conflict.

Admitting that the reason the Republicans lost was the Iran war, the US vice president wrote, “Everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there.”

He added: “I remain hopeful about our country. To the people who are pissed off and want to say, ‘I told you so’: you’re right, you did tell us so. Take that energy into electing Republicans who share your worldview. To the people who are just pissed at the results, you should be. Let’s take that anger and get back to the work of saving our country.”

headline: At Tehran rally, some Iranians doubt US midterm result would make a difference for them
description: Majid Heidari, a 62-year-old fabric producer, argued the resulting rise in oil prices had “impacted the American...
article_text:
Majid Heidari, a 62-year-old fabric producer, argued the resulting rise in oil prices had “impacted the American vote”, as thousands gathered in Tehran for an annual anti-US rally, AFP reports.

“When Europe and the US unite against us, we must use our tool (closing Hormuz),” he said.

“There is nothing we can do but put some pressure on governments by making their own people feel the consequences.”

Still, he doubted the US election result would really change much for ordinary Iranians. Mohammad, a 42-year-old civil servant, shared this view. “I believe whether it is the Democrats or the Republicans, there is no difference for us,” he said.

headline: Rizwan stages resounding comeback in domestic cricket after England tour controversy
description: Wicketkeeper-batter finishes the day unbeaten on 200 off 252 balls, hitting 35 fours and one six.
author: Dawn Sport
article_text:
Mohammad Rizwan made a commanding unbeaten double century on the second day of the opening round of the Quaid-i-Azam Trophy Gold tournament, putting Peshawar Blues in a strong position against Faisalabad at the Abbottabad Cricket Stadium and delivering a timely response after a turbulent period following Pakistan’s disastrous Test series in England.

The wicketkeeper-batter, who was among seven players sent home after the second Test at Lord’s and remains under investigation by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency over matters linked to the tour, finished the day unbeaten on 200 off 252 balls, hitting 35 fours and one six.

His innings helped Peshawar declare at 503 for four in 115.2 overs after resuming the day at 306 for three. Overnight centurion Najab Khan scored 133, while Mohammad Haris contributed an unbeaten 70 off 69 balls, including nine fours and two sixes.

Rizwan’s innings marked a significant personal milestone — his second double century in first-class cricket — and came shortly after the Pakistan Cricket Board cleared him to resume domestic cricket.

The former Test regular had endured a lean run with the bat in England, scoring just 61 runs in four innings before the squad overhaul and subsequent investigation into alleged dressing-room issues and related matters.

In reply, Faisalabad reached 118 for two in 35.2 overs at stumps. Both openers, Faham-ul-Haq (31) and Sameer Saqib (25), were dismissed leg-before-wicket by Mohammad Adnan.

Asim Ali Nasir (35 not out) and Atiq-ur-Rehman (24 not out) will resume their innings on Thursday.

Lean outing for Babar

Elsewhere, Babar Azam endured another modest outing, scoring just 28 as Lahore Whites were bowled out for 234 in 49.2 overs against Fata at the Diamond Cricket Ground in Islamabad, conceding a first-innings lead of 128 runs.

Fata had earlier been dismissed for 362, with debutant Fawad Arshad scoring 115. Teenage fast bowler Hammad Aziz claimed six for 97 for Lahore Whites.

Shaheen Shah Afridi and Afaq Afridi took three wickets apiece for Fata, with the latter dismissing Babar. Fata ended the day at 22 for one.

At the Shoaib Akhtar Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi, Multan recovered from a middle-order collapse that left them struggling at 88 for five to reach 249 for seven in reply to Islamabad’s 215.

Imran Rafiq led the recovery with an unbeaten 93, while Sharoon Siraj scored 82. Musa Khan took three for 31 for the hosts.

At the National Ground in Islamabad, Karachi Blues scored 280 to secure a slender first-innings lead of 39 runs over Sialkot Blues, who closed the day at 13 without loss. Mohammad Ghazi Ghori top-scored for Karachi with 88.

Mohammad Rizwan made a commanding unbeaten double century on the second day of the opening round of the Quaid-i-Azam Trophy Gold tournament, putting Peshawar Blues in a strong position against Faisalabad at the Abbottabad Cricket Stadium and delivering a timely response after a turbulent period following Pakistan’s disastrous Test series in England.

The wicketkeeper-batter, who was among seven players sent home after the second Test at Lord’s and remains under investigation by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency over matters linked to the tour, finished the day unbeaten on 200 off 252 balls, hitting 35 fours and one six.

His innings helped Peshawar declare at 503 for four in 115.2 overs after resuming the day at 306 for three. Overnight centurion Najab Khan scored 133, while Mohammad Haris contributed an unbeaten 70 off 69 balls, including nine fours and two sixes.

Rizwan’s innings marked a significant personal milestone — his second double century in first-class cricket — and came shortly after the Pakistan Cricket Board cleared him to resume domestic cricket.

The former Test regular had endured a lean run with the bat in England, scoring just 61 runs in four innings before the squad overhaul and subsequent investigation into alleged dressing-room issues and related matters.

In reply, Faisalabad reached 118 for two in 35.2 overs at stumps. Both openers, Faham-ul-Haq (31) and Sameer Saqib (25), were dismissed leg-before-wicket by Mohammad Adnan.

Asim Ali Nasir (35 not out) and Atiq-ur-Rehman (24 not out) will resume their innings on Thursday.

Lean outing for Babar

Elsewhere, Babar Azam endured another modest outing, scoring just 28 as Lahore Whites were bowled out for 234 in 49.2 overs against Fata at the Diamond Cricket Ground in Islamabad, conceding a first-innings lead of 128 runs.

Fata had earlier been dismissed for 362, with debutant Fawad Arshad scoring 115. Teenage fast bowler Hammad Aziz claimed six for 97 for Lahore Whites.

Shaheen Shah Afridi and Afaq Afridi took three wickets apiece for Fata, with the latter dismissing Babar. Fata ended the day at 22 for one.

At the Shoaib Akhtar Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi, Multan recovered from a middle-order collapse that left them struggling at 88 for five to reach 249 for seven in reply to Islamabad’s 215.

Imran Rafiq led the recovery with an unbeaten 93, while Sharoon Siraj scored 82. Musa Khan took three for 31 for the hosts.

At the National Ground in Islamabad, Karachi Blues scored 280 to secure a slender first-innings lead of 39 runs over Sialkot Blues, who closed the day at 13 without loss. Mohammad Ghazi Ghori top-scored for Karachi with 88.

headline: Asif says Chaudhry Salik's remarks about corruption in Punjab 'beyond my understanding'
description: Marriyum Aurangzeb calls on the PML-Q minister to either fulfil his responsibilities or step down from his role.
author: News Desk
article_text:
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said on Wednesday that Minister for Overseas Pakistanis Chaudhry Salik Hussain’s remarks regarding corruption in Punjab were “beyond my understanding”.

During a talk show on a private television channel on Monday, the Pakistan Muslim League-Quaid (PML-Q) leader had lavished praise on former Punjab chief minister Chaudhry Pervez Elahi. However, he had also criticised the present provincial administration, headed by Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, alleging that he regularly heard complaints of corruption.

On Tuesday, CM Maryam had sent a Rs5 billion defamation notice to the minister, demanding that he retract his remarks.

In a post on the social media platform X on Wednesday, Asif said, “Chaudhry Salik Sahib is very respected in my eyes; I respect his elders just as I respect my own.

“His statement regarding corruption in Punjab is beyond my limited political understanding. Corruption is the biggest issue in our society and it is the collective responsibility of the political leadership, both at the central and provincial levels, to rid the country of this curse,” he said.

He went on to say that Salik was a part of “both the federal and provincial governments and the leadership of both these governments lies with the PML-N”.

“If this statement is part of some future political agenda — to target Maryam Nawaz’s government and carve out space for himself in Punjab and at the Centre to secure his political future — then it starts to make sense,” Asif said.

He also praised Maryam’s performance, saying her work across Punjab’s cities and villages and the service standards being set by her government would pose a “very difficult challenge” for its opponents.

Meanwhile, Punjab Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb sought an apology from Salik over his comments, saying that the PML-Q leader was “himself admitting that he has no evidence to support the allegations he made regarding corruption in the Punjab government”.

“After this, what dignity, justice, and principles demand is clear: an apology should be sought for the lack of evidence and for making baseless allegations, rather than turning the transfer of a single DC into an issue of personal ego,” she wrote.

The Punjab minister called on Salik to either fulfil his responsibilities as a minister or step down from his role “instead of engaging in empty rhetoric about eradicating corruption from society and promoting good governance”.

“We will not tolerate false and baseless allegations against the chief minister who has set an example of serving the people in Pakistan through hard work and transparency in two and a half years,” Aurangzeb asserted.

Acknowledging that corruption existed as a “disease in every society in the world”, she contended that Punjab was the only province where the chief minister herself was “leading the campaign to eliminate corruption”.

What did Salik say?

During his interview, Salik had also questioned lavish government spending, particularly the use of official aircraft, arguing that public representatives should remain mindful of the country’s economic difficulties. Officials using government aircraft, he said, should be required to demonstrate the tangible outcomes and public benefits of their trips.

He further called for greater ministerial accountability, proposing that the federal as well as provincial ministers should be empowered to perform their duties, but also be held answerable for their performance.

The remarks carry particular political significance given the fractured relationship between the Chaudhry family and the PTI leadership. Salik, the younger son of PML-Q president Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain, belongs to a family whose political loyalties have diverged sharply since the ouster of Imran Khan’s government in 2022 through a no-confidence vote.

While Elahi and his son, former federal minister Moonis Elahi, aligned themselves with the PTI, the Shujaat family chose to stand with the Sharifs. Salik’s elder brother, Shafay Hussain, is also part of CM Maryam’s cabinet in Punjab.

On Tuesday, CM Maryam said the PML-Q leader’s anger stemmed from neither corruption nor progress. She said the issue was that she had changed the deputy commissioner of Gujrat a few days earlier, whereas Salik wanted a DC of his choice to be appointed.

The defamation notice — sent to Salik, ARY News host Naeem Ashraf Butt and the channel’s chairman — said the minister’s remarks were not just an expression of disagreement with policy or “ordinary political criticism”, but conveyed “serious imputations” of widespread corruption in the province.

The notice called on them to retract the remarks, publish an “unconditional and unequivocal apology and clarification” and “remove or suitably correct” the portions of the interview in question. It also demanded a sum of Rs5bn in damages.

Meanwhile, responding to Maryam’s remarks, Salik said he stood by his statement and had responded honestly to a question during the interview.

The minister’s remarks had also drawn a sharp rebuttal from Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari, who advised Salik not to “bite the hand that feeds him”. Bokhari also alleged that his displeasure stemmed from a request to appoint a deputy commissioner of his choice being turned down.

Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said on Wednesday that Minister for Overseas Pakistanis Chaudhry Salik Hussain’s remarks regarding corruption in Punjab were “beyond my understanding”.

During a talk show on a private television channel on Monday, the Pakistan Muslim League-Quaid (PML-Q) leader had lavished praise on former Punjab chief minister Chaudhry Pervez Elahi. However, he had also criticised the present provincial administration, headed by Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, alleging that he regularly heard complaints of corruption.

On Tuesday, CM Maryam had sent a Rs5 billion defamation notice to the minister, demanding that he retract his remarks.

In a post on the social media platform X on Wednesday, Asif said, “Chaudhry Salik Sahib is very respected in my eyes; I respect his elders just as I respect my own.

“His statement regarding corruption in Punjab is beyond my limited political understanding. Corruption is the biggest issue in our society and it is the collective responsibility of the political leadership, both at the central and provincial levels, to rid the country of this curse,” he said.

He went on to say that Salik was a part of “both the federal and provincial governments and the leadership of both these governments lies with the PML-N”.

“If this statement is part of some future political agenda — to target Maryam Nawaz’s government and carve out space for himself in Punjab and at the Centre to secure his political future — then it starts to make sense,” Asif said.

He also praised Maryam’s performance, saying her work across Punjab’s cities and villages and the service standards being set by her government would pose a “very difficult challenge” for its opponents.

Meanwhile, Punjab Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb sought an apology from Salik over his comments, saying that the PML-Q leader was “himself admitting that he has no evidence to support the allegations he made regarding corruption in the Punjab government”.

“After this, what dignity, justice, and principles demand is clear: an apology should be sought for the lack of evidence and for making baseless allegations, rather than turning the transfer of a single DC into an issue of personal ego,” she wrote.

The Punjab minister called on Salik to either fulfil his responsibilities as a minister or step down from his role “instead of engaging in empty rhetoric about eradicating corruption from society and promoting good governance”.

“We will not tolerate false and baseless allegations against the chief minister who has set an example of serving the people in Pakistan through hard work and transparency in two and a half years,” Aurangzeb asserted.

Acknowledging that corruption existed as a “disease in every society in the world”, she contended that Punjab was the only province where the chief minister herself was “leading the campaign to eliminate corruption”.

What did Salik say?

During his interview, Salik had also questioned lavish government spending, particularly the use of official aircraft, arguing that public representatives should remain mindful of the country’s economic difficulties. Officials using government aircraft, he said, should be required to demonstrate the tangible outcomes and public benefits of their trips.

He further called for greater ministerial accountability, proposing that the federal as well as provincial ministers should be empowered to perform their duties, but also be held answerable for their performance.

The remarks carry particular political significance given the fractured relationship between the Chaudhry family and the PTI leadership. Salik, the younger son of PML-Q president Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain, belongs to a family whose political loyalties have diverged sharply since the ouster of Imran Khan’s government in 2022 through a no-confidence vote.

While Elahi and his son, former federal minister Moonis Elahi, aligned themselves with the PTI, the Shujaat family chose to stand with the Sharifs. Salik’s elder brother, Shafay Hussain, is also part of CM Maryam’s cabinet in Punjab.

On Tuesday, CM Maryam said the PML-Q leader’s anger stemmed from neither corruption nor progress. She said the issue was that she had changed the deputy commissioner of Gujrat a few days earlier, whereas Salik wanted a DC of his choice to be appointed.

The defamation notice — sent to Salik, ARY News host Naeem Ashraf Butt and the channel’s chairman — said the minister’s remarks were not just an expression of disagreement with policy or “ordinary political criticism”, but conveyed “serious imputations” of widespread corruption in the province.

The notice called on them to retract the remarks, publish an “unconditional and unequivocal apology and clarification” and “remove or suitably correct” the portions of the interview in question. It also demanded a sum of Rs5bn in damages.

Meanwhile, responding to Maryam’s remarks, Salik said he stood by his statement and had responded honestly to a question during the interview.

The minister’s remarks had also drawn a sharp rebuttal from Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari, who advised Salik not to “bite the hand that feeds him”. Bokhari also alleged that his displeasure stemmed from a request to appoint a deputy commissioner of his choice being turned down.

headline: Iran protests 'biased' reports on shipping security by global body: state media
description: Iran has slammed “biased” reports on the ongoing shipping crisis by the International Maritime Organisation (IMO),...
article_text:
Iran has slammed “biased” reports on the ongoing shipping crisis by the International Maritime Organisation (IMO), emphasising that seafarer protection should not be selective and that difficult conditions facing Iranian sailors must also be addressed, state news agency IRNA reports.

At the 138th session of the IMO Council in London, the Iranian delegation has slammed “the organisation’s incomplete and unbalanced reports on maritime security and seafarer protection”, demanding an impartial assessment of threats to maritime safety.

It stresses that IMO reports should not overlook the US naval blockade of Iranian ports, as well as military attacks on vessels and maritime infrastructure.

headline: Oil tumbles as investors weigh end to Iran war after Democrats sweep US midterm elections
description: Oil prices have fallen below $100 a barrel in volatile trading as investors await Washington’s next move in the...
article_text:
Oil prices have fallen below $100 a barrel in volatile trading as investors await Washington’s next move in the US-Israeli war with Iran after President Donald Trump’s Republican Party lost control of Congress in midterm elections, Reuters reports.

Brent futures were down $4.50, or 4.3 per cent, to $99.07 a barrel at 1619 GMT (9:19pm, PKT), while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures are down $4.13, or 4.3pc, to $92.02.

headline: In meeting with Iranian ambassador, Dar highlights importance of dialogue, diplomacy for regional peace: FO
description: Iranian Ambassador Reza Amiri Moghadam has called on Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar at the...
article_text:
Iranian Ambassador Reza Amiri Moghadam has called on Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar at the foreign ministry, where the two discussed regional developments as well as bilateral relations, the Foreign Office (FO) says.

Dar “reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening its close and brotherly ties with Iran” and underscored the importance of dialogue and diplomacy to promote regional peace and stability, it adds.

headline: Govt says Islamabad's One Constitution Avenue to be turned into a five-star hotel
description: Ahsan Iqbal says the JIT has recommended the project be started anew and auctioned in a transparent manner; Mohsin Naqvi says government to make "rightful payments to occupants".
author: News Desk
article_text:
The federal government on Wednesday said that a joint investigation team had revealed that Islamabad’s One Constitution Avenue was built on “irregularities and rigging” and announced that the residential building will soon be turned into a five-star hotel.

The building, a skyscraper in the federal capital that houses residential apartments, had its lease cancelled by the Capital Development Authority (CDA) due to the company behind the project defaulting on payments. The decision was upheld by the Islamabad High Court (IHC) in April.

The building was initially supposed to be a five-star hotel project; however, instead of functioning as a five-star hotel, it was converted into residential apartments and commercial areas. The IHC’s order led to the mass evictions of residents in May, following which Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif formed a joint investigation team (JIT) to probe the matter.

Addressing a press conference on Wednesday alongside Information Minister Attaullah Tarar and State Minister for Interior Tallal Chaudhry, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal said the JIT presented its report to the federal cabinet today, noting that the project was fraudulent.

He said that the report had input from the National Accountability Bureau (NAB), the Federal Investigation Agency, the Federal Board of Revenue, the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan, the Intelligence Bureau and Inter-Services Intelligence.

“They carefully assessed this project and presented the report, and it was approved,” Iqbal said. “The JIT has clearly identified that the project was created based on irregularity and rigging and that the bidding process was manipulated.”

Iqbal added that, according to the report, rules were ignored to provide benefits and the company which was given the lease had no rightful claim.

“In this whole matter, the CDA was found complicit, and similarly, the conditions of the bank guarantee were removed to provide benefits to the developers,” he stated. “The work which was carried out was conducted in a very suspicious manner and the apartments were sold illegally.”

He noted that the project was initially approved as a five-star hotel two decades ago, but later it was turned into apartments.

“The JIT has identified Abdul Hafeez Sheikh, who has been called the mastermind and was found to be in connivance with CDA officials,” the planning minister added.

“CDA officers such as Kamran Lashari, who was chairman at the time, Dr Faisal Awan, Azhar Ali Chaudhry, Brigadier (retired) Nasrullah and Marhoom Rai Nawaz Kharal were found to be colluding in fraud,” he said.

Iqbal said that as a result of the scheme, the national exchequer suffered losses, while the aforementioned people “gained financially and defrauded the Pakistani people of their invested capital”.

“The JIT recommended that Sheikh and his company be blacklisted from future public projects and that proceedings be launched against him,” the minister added.

It was further recommended that the project be reviewed and work undertaken to achieve its original purpose as a hotel. Additionally, the report recommended that the project be started anew and auctioned in a transparent manner, he said.

“Security clearance and clearance from other institutions should also be sought so that future projects have a steady framework to prevent this type of fraud from happening again,” Iqbal said, adding that fire safety and other protocols must also be ensured.

He added that according to the JIT, the project should be renamed, as the name ‘One Constitution Avenue’ was the same address as the finance ministry.

“They used this address for marketing purposes only,” the minister asserted.

“There will be action taken against those found involved in fraud. The government has a responsibility to protect those who were robbed or swindled.”

Iqbal said it was decided that those defrauded would receive compensation, their principal investments would be refunded and payments would be adjusted against their Kibor interest “so they do not suffer losses”.

“It was also recommended that the CDA and its ordinance be overhauled and that an independent master plan commission be formed to shut the door on such fraud in the future,” he announced.

Iqbal added that all of the records must be digitised and officers should be rotated between the state planning, enforcement and building control departments every two years.

“People have held offices for 20 years and opened offices of fraud. With this constant rotation, it will close the door on these corrupt projects,” he explained.

“In the same way, pre-audit auctions and contracts from third parties will be consulted, and in light of this JIT report, NAB has been ordered to take action against anyone involved in this project, and those who facilitated it,” Iqbal said.

Meanwhile, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also addressed a press conference on Wednesday and said that the government had now regained possession of the skyscraper, vowing to turn the building into a five-star hotel within months.

“In official documents, we always had possession of this building, and after the cabinet’s approval, it is now legally in our possession,” Naqvi maintained.

He regretted that the government’s decision to regain control of the building earlier this year had been portrayed as a “crime”, decrying how Islamabad’s land had been infringed upon.

“We will try our best to convert this building into a five-star hotel in months,” the interior minister announced, reaffirming that this had been the project’s primary objective.

“There is a severe shortage of hotels in Islamabad. We will soon try to make an agreement with a large chain of hotels and convert this building into a five-star hotel,” he stated.

He commended the CDA chairman and legal team for pursuing this case; however, Naqvi also reproached the CDA for being at fault.

“NAB will tell who is responsible,” he said.

“As per JIT recommendations, we will try to make rightful payments to the occupants,” Naqvi said. “This is binding for us after the report.”

The interior minister said he was grateful to PM Shehbaz, recalling that the prime minister had assured him that the right decision would be taken.

Naqvi further said that a residents’ committee, which was overseeing the building’s affairs, had been abolished.

“A CDA member will look after the building’s matters from now on,” he said, reiterating that the hotel would be operational soon and be a “gift to the people of Islamabad”.

article_html:
The federal government on Wednesday said that a joint investigation team had revealed that Islamabad’s One Constitution Avenue was built on “irregularities and rigging” and announced that the residential building will soon be turned into a five-star hotel.

The building, a skyscraper in the federal capital that houses residential apartments, had its lease cancelled by the Capital Development Authority (CDA) due to the company behind the project defaulting on payments. The decision was upheld by the Islamabad High Court (IHC) in April.

The building was initially supposed to be a five-star hotel project; however, instead of functioning as a five-star hotel, it was converted into residential apartments and commercial areas. The IHC’s order led to the mass evictions of residents in May, following which Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif formed a joint investigation team (JIT) to probe the matter.

Addressing a press conference on Wednesday alongside Information Minister Attaullah Tarar and State Minister for Interior Tallal Chaudhry, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal said the JIT presented its report to the federal cabinet today, noting that the project was fraudulent.

He said that the report had input from the National Accountability Bureau (NAB), the Federal Investigation Agency, the Federal Board of Revenue, the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan, the Intelligence Bureau and Inter-Services Intelligence.

“They carefully assessed this project and presented the report, and it was approved,” Iqbal said. “The JIT has clearly identified that the project was created based on irregularity and rigging and that the bidding process was manipulated.”

Iqbal added that, according to the report, rules were ignored to provide benefits and the company which was given the lease had no rightful claim.

“In this whole matter, the CDA was found complicit, and similarly, the conditions of the bank guarantee were removed to provide benefits to the developers,” he stated. “The work which was carried out was conducted in a very suspicious manner and the apartments were sold illegally.”

He noted that the project was initially approved as a five-star hotel two decades ago, but later it was turned into apartments.

“The JIT has identified Abdul Hafeez Sheikh, who has been called the mastermind and was found to be in connivance with CDA officials,” the planning minister added.

“CDA officers such as Kamran Lashari, who was chairman at the time, Dr Faisal Awan, Azhar Ali Chaudhry, Brigadier (retired) Nasrullah and Marhoom Rai Nawaz Kharal were found to be colluding in fraud,” he said.

Iqbal said that as a result of the scheme, the national exchequer suffered losses, while the aforementioned people “gained financially and defrauded the Pakistani people of their invested capital”.

“The JIT recommended that Sheikh and his company be blacklisted from future public projects and that proceedings be launched against him,” the minister added.

It was further recommended that the project be reviewed and work undertaken to achieve its original purpose as a hotel. Additionally, the report recommended that the project be started anew and auctioned in a transparent manner, he said.

“Security clearance and clearance from other institutions should also be sought so that future projects have a steady framework to prevent this type of fraud from happening again,” Iqbal said, adding that fire safety and other protocols must also be ensured.

He added that according to the JIT, the project should be renamed, as the name ‘One Constitution Avenue’ was the same address as the finance ministry.

“They used this address for marketing purposes only,” the minister asserted.

“There will be action taken against those found involved in fraud. The government has a responsibility to protect those who were robbed or swindled.”

Iqbal said it was decided that those defrauded would receive compensation, their principal investments would be refunded and payments would be adjusted against their Kibor interest “so they do not suffer losses”.

“It was also recommended that the CDA and its ordinance be overhauled and that an independent master plan commission be formed to shut the door on such fraud in the future,” he announced.

Iqbal added that all of the records must be digitised and officers should be rotated between the state planning, enforcement and building control departments every two years.

“People have held offices for 20 years and opened offices of fraud. With this constant rotation, it will close the door on these corrupt projects,” he explained.

“In the same way, pre-audit auctions and contracts from third parties will be consulted, and in light of this JIT report, NAB has been ordered to take action against anyone involved in this project, and those who facilitated it,” Iqbal said.

Meanwhile, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also addressed a press conference on Wednesday and said that the government had now regained possession of the skyscraper, vowing to turn the building into a five-star hotel within months.

“In official documents, we always had possession of this building, and after the cabinet’s approval, it is now legally in our possession,” Naqvi maintained.

He regretted that the government’s decision to regain control of the building earlier this year had been portrayed as a “crime”, decrying how Islamabad’s land had been infringed upon.

“We will try our best to convert this building into a five-star hotel in months,” the interior minister announced, reaffirming that this had been the project’s primary objective.

“There is a severe shortage of hotels in Islamabad. We will soon try to make an agreement with a large chain of hotels and convert this building into a five-star hotel,” he stated.

He commended the CDA chairman and legal team for pursuing this case; however, Naqvi also reproached the CDA for being at fault.

“NAB will tell who is responsible,” he said.

“As per JIT recommendations, we will try to make rightful payments to the occupants,” Naqvi said. “This is binding for us after the report.”

The interior minister said he was grateful to PM Shehbaz, recalling that the prime minister had assured him that the right decision would be taken.

Naqvi further said that a residents’ committee, which was overseeing the building’s affairs, had been abolished.

“A CDA member will look after the building’s matters from now on,” he said, reiterating that the hotel would be operational soon and be a “gift to the people of Islamabad”.

headline: ICRC says delivered its first medical aid into Yemen's besieged Taiz in weeks
description: The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) says it has brought medical supplies into Yemen’s Taiz for the...
article_text:
The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) says it has brought medical supplies into Yemen’s Taiz for the first time in weeks since the Houthis surrounded the city, AFP reports.

The ICRC “delivered four trucks of essential medical supplies to Taiz city, including surgical kits to help hospitals treat weapon-wounded patients,” it says in a statement.

“This is the ICRC’s first delivery of medical supplies to hospitals in Taiz City since 23 September, just before the intensification of fighting in the area,” ICRC spokesman Hachem Osseiran tells AFP.

headline: Iran handed Trump a strategic defeat on the battlefield, political defeat in Washington, national security chief says

The Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, Mohsen Rezaei, has commented on the Democrats sweeping the US midterm elections, saying that the Iranian nation “handed Trump a strategic defeat on the battlefield and in the Hormuz — and a political defeat in Washington”.

“Meanwhile, Americans got stuck with the bill for his war,” he writes on X.

He warns that anyone who takes on Iran “will pay the price — from the battlefield to their own doorstep”.

headline: Israel president urges compromise after divisive election
description: Herzog says both sides need to accept that “not every commitment and promise can be fulfilled” and to avoid new elections.
author: AFP
article_text:
Israel’s president on Wednesday opened talks on forming a new government with a call for compromise, saying neither side had won divisive elections, as he also condemned “racist” rhetoric against Arab parties that made sharp gains.

More than a week after Israel’s first election since the October 7, 2023 Hamas attacks, President Isaac Herzog began meeting party leaders to decide whether to give Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu or his rival Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form a government in the deeply polarised country.

With neither bloc holding a majority in the 120-seat parliament after the Oct 27 vote, Herzog said both sides needed to accept that “not every commitment and promise can be fulfilled” and to avoid new elections.

“In the current reality, in which there is no clear winner after the elections, I ask for originality and creativity, courage and goodwill, so that the State of Israel emerges the winner,” Herzog said.

The election saw soaring support for lists from the Arab minority, descendants of Palestinians who stayed in Israel after its 1948 creation and who have often been outraged by the harsh rhetoric and actions of Netanyahu’s hard-right government.

Netanyahu has gone on the offensive against Arab-majority lists, who have the power to put Eisenkot in power if they team up.

Netanyahu has pointed to the arrests of several people with envelopes of cash on election day in what authorities called localised incidents, and accused leaders of accepting money from Qatar, an allegation also levelled against the prime minister’s own aides.

Without naming any leader, Herzog, whose role is usually ceremonial, said he had “great respect” for the Arab minority, which makes up around 20 per cent of Israel’s population.

“I condemn the coarseness and racist expressions that we have heard recently. There is no place for them (to be made) toward any community in Israel,” Herzog said.

No evidence found

The Central Elections Committee said it had conducted an audit of 9,069 polling stations following complaints and found no evidence that would question the results’ integrity.

The committee, which reflects the makeup of the outgoing parliament, approved the results with 15 members in favour and two against but 14 others abstaining.

Itamar Ben Gvir, the ultra-nationalist national security minister known for his provocative calls for Palestinian suffering, said his party did not accept the results and he urged the arrest of Arab-Israeli party leaders.

Several Israeli media outlets said authorities were investigating Arab lawmaker Ayman Odeh for allegedly taking foreign money. He is part of the largest Arab group, the Joint List, which in a statement denounced “political persecution”.

Eisenkot, a former military chief who has vowed to turn the page on Netanyahu’s long, divisive reign, accused the prime minister of trying to “undermine Israeli democracy” and inflame sentiment against elected officials.

“We will not allow the State of Israel to be dragged into a dark abyss, far beyond the bounds of democratic conduct,” Eisenkot said, as he marked the 1995 assassination of prime minister Yitzhak Rabin.

Buoyed by US elections

Eisenkot has warned Netanyahu against launching a new war with his ally US President Donald Trump against Iran, which could help the Israeli prime minister push for a unity government or to run out the clock until new elections.

Opposition lawmakers said Tuesday’s midterm elections in the United States, in which Democrats trounced Trump’s Republicans, reinforced the need to remove Netanyahu.

Democrats have vowed a tougher line on Israel amid outrage over the devastation wrought by the assault on Gaza. Trump said as voting was underway that he had agreed with Netanyahu to end nearly $4 billion in annual US military aid to Israel by the end of the year.

“The continued tenure of Netanyahu and Ben Gvir could lead Israel down a path of international sanctions, international isolation and a clash with the US, our friend and most important ally,” said Yair Golan, who heads the most left-wing party within the opposition bloc.

Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister who has been in power on and off for nearly two decades, has called for a “broad national government” — with himself at the top. He faces corruption charges that could land him in jail if he leaves office.

Herzog’s statements have raised speculation that he could sound out leaders on a possible unity government, but Eisenkot and his allies have ruled that out.

Herzog will hold an initial two days of consultations and then give a contender 28 days to form a government, with a potential 14-day extension.

It took Netanyahu, who at the time had a better showing by Likud, 58 days to form a government after the last election in November 2022.

Israel held five elections between 2019 and 2022 after repeated deadlocks.

article_html:
Israel’s president on Wednesday opened talks on forming a new government with a call for compromise, saying neither side had won divisive elections, as he also condemned “racist” rhetoric against Arab parties that made sharp gains.

More than a week after Israel’s first election since the October 7, 2023 Hamas attacks, President Isaac Herzog began meeting party leaders to decide whether to give Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu or his rival Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form a government in the deeply polarised country.

With neither bloc holding a majority in the 120-seat parliament after the Oct 27 vote, Herzog said both sides needed to accept that “not every commitment and promise can be fulfilled” and to avoid new elections.

“In the current reality, in which there is no clear winner after the elections, I ask for originality and creativity, courage and goodwill, so that the State of Israel emerges the winner,” Herzog said.

The election saw soaring support for lists from the Arab minority, descendants of Palestinians who stayed in Israel after its 1948 creation and who have often been outraged by the harsh rhetoric and actions of Netanyahu’s hard-right government.

Netanyahu has gone on the offensive against Arab-majority lists, who have the power to put Eisenkot in power if they team up.

Netanyahu has pointed to the arrests of several people with envelopes of cash on election day in what authorities called localised incidents, and accused leaders of accepting money from Qatar, an allegation also levelled against the prime minister’s own aides.

Without naming any leader, Herzog, whose role is usually ceremonial, said he had “great respect” for the Arab minority, which makes up around 20 per cent of Israel’s population.

“I condemn the coarseness and racist expressions that we have heard recently. There is no place for them (to be made) toward any community in Israel,” Herzog said.

No evidence found

The Central Elections Committee said it had conducted an audit of 9,069 polling stations following complaints and found no evidence that would question the results’ integrity.

The committee, which reflects the makeup of the outgoing parliament, approved the results with 15 members in favour and two against but 14 others abstaining.

Itamar Ben Gvir, the ultra-nationalist national security minister known for his provocative calls for Palestinian suffering, said his party did not accept the results and he urged the arrest of Arab-Israeli party leaders.

Several Israeli media outlets said authorities were investigating Arab lawmaker Ayman Odeh for allegedly taking foreign money. He is part of the largest Arab group, the Joint List, which in a statement denounced “political persecution”.

Eisenkot, a former military chief who has vowed to turn the page on Netanyahu’s long, divisive reign, accused the prime minister of trying to “undermine Israeli democracy” and inflame sentiment against elected officials.

“We will not allow the State of Israel to be dragged into a dark abyss, far beyond the bounds of democratic conduct,” Eisenkot said, as he marked the 1995 assassination of prime minister Yitzhak Rabin.

Buoyed by US elections

Eisenkot has warned Netanyahu against launching a new war with his ally US President Donald Trump against Iran, which could help the Israeli prime minister push for a unity government or to run out the clock until new elections.

Opposition lawmakers said Tuesday’s midterm elections in the United States, in which Democrats trounced Trump’s Republicans, reinforced the need to remove Netanyahu.

Democrats have vowed a tougher line on Israel amid outrage over the devastation wrought by the assault on Gaza. Trump said as voting was underway that he had agreed with Netanyahu to end nearly $4 billion in annual US military aid to Israel by the end of the year.

“The continued tenure of Netanyahu and Ben Gvir could lead Israel down a path of international sanctions, international isolation and a clash with the US, our friend and most important ally,” said Yair Golan, who heads the most left-wing party within the opposition bloc.

Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister who has been in power on and off for nearly two decades, has called for a “broad national government” — with himself at the top. He faces corruption charges that could land him in jail if he leaves office.

Herzog’s statements have raised speculation that he could sound out leaders on a possible unity government, but Eisenkot and his allies have ruled that out.

Herzog will hold an initial two days of consultations and then give a contender 28 days to form a government, with a potential 14-day extension.

It took Netanyahu, who at the time had a better showing by Likud, 58 days to form a government after the last election in November 2022.

Israel held five elections between 2019 and 2022 after repeated deadlocks.

headline: Fuel prices
Govt cuts petrol price by Rs5.45 per litre, high-speed diesel by Rs3.68
description: Petrol will retail at Rs369.06 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs391.28 on Wednesday; reduction comes as global oil prices slide 2pc.
author: News Desk
article_text:
The government on Tuesday reduced the price of petrol by Rs5.45 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.68.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs369.06 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs391.52.

The prices are applicable for Nov 4 (Wednesday), according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

The latest price cut also comes as international oil prices slid about 2 per cent to a three-week low on Tuesday in volatile trade. The market weighed talks to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran against worries about additional supply disruptions from recent attacks in both conflicts.

Brent futures fell $1.63, or 2pc, to $103.14 a barrel at 8:44pm PKT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude fell 67 cents, or 1pc, to $95.79. Brent was on track for its lowest close since Oct 7 and WTI was headed for its lowest close since Oct 14.

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Monday for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This would allow a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

Addressing a press conference today, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said efforts were being made to introduce a similar system for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

He also hinted at the latest reduction in fuel prices, saying “even better news will come before us”.

The Jamaat-i-Islami and the government also held another round of talks to discuss possible relief to low-income citizens in petroleum prices, and agreed to continue their negotiations in the coming days.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

On Sept 13, PM Shehbaz also announced a “relief scheme” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, the petroleum minister announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

article_html:
The government on Tuesday reduced the price of petrol by Rs5.45 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.68.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs369.06 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs391.52.

The prices are applicable for Nov 4 (Wednesday), according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

The latest price cut also comes as international oil prices slid about 2 per cent to a three-week low on Tuesday in volatile trade. The market weighed talks to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran against worries about additional supply disruptions from recent attacks in both conflicts.

Brent futures fell $1.63, or 2pc, to $103.14 a barrel at 8:44pm PKT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude fell 67 cents, or 1pc, to $95.79. Brent was on track for its lowest close since Oct 7 and WTI was headed for its lowest close since Oct 14.

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Monday for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This would allow a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

Addressing a press conference today, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said efforts were being made to introduce a similar system for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

He also hinted at the latest reduction in fuel prices, saying “even better news will come before us”.

The Jamaat-i-Islami and the government also held another round of talks to discuss possible relief to low-income citizens in petroleum prices, and agreed to continue their negotiations in the coming days.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

On Sept 13, PM Shehbaz also announced a “relief scheme” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, the petroleum minister announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

Additional input by Reuters

headline: 38 briefly detained in Karachi as police baton-charge protesters headed towards CM House
description: Police say protesters, mainly teachers making demands related to service structure, turned violent and pelted officials with stones.
author: Imtiaz Ali
article_text:
KARACHI: Thirty-eight people were released after brief detention on Wednesday as police used tear gas and batons against protesting teachers headed towards Chief Minister House from Karachi Press Club (KPC).

Hundreds of teachers had gathered outside the press club at the call of the All Sindh Primary Teachers Association (ASPTA). They were headed towards CM House to present their demands that pertained to the service structure and called for delegating powers for transfers and postings to district officers.

The protesters chanted slogans and attempted to move towards the CM House. However, when they arrived near Fawara Chowk, police baton-charged them and used tear gas shells to push them back toward the press club.

Adjoining roads near the KPC were closed to traffic, according to a traffic police spokesperson.

South Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Syed Asad Raza told Dawn that all detained teachers “have been released at night”, after he confirmed in earlier comments that 38 people were taken into custody.

Speaking to Dawn earlier in the day, the DIG noted that a teachers’ organisation had announced a protest at the KPC, with a march planned toward the CM House.

He said prior to the protest, the administration made concerted efforts to resolve the matter through negotiations and engaged officials from the education department to facilitate meaningful dialogue.

The official said the protest leadership was categorically told that entry into the Red Zone — a term used to denote the area surrounding Governor House and Chief Minister House — would not be permitted. Nevertheless, the administration was directed to exhaust all available resources and make every effort to ensure a peaceful resolution through dialogue, he said.

Raza alleged that around 3:15pm, the protesters turned “violent, abandoned the course of negotiations and forcibly started advancing towards the CM House.”

He claimed that the protesting teachers “breached police barricades and resorted to pelting police personnel with stones, causing injuries to one official.”

“Upon reaching and crossing Kabir Masjid on Governor House Road, the situation escalated, compelling police to resort to shelling to disperse the violent mob and restore order,” said the South police chief.

He said during the operation, 38 protesters, including ASPTA President Ghulam Rasool Mahar and General Secretary Aijaz Ali Chandio, were taken into custody.

Raza insisted that police took drastic action as the teachers tried to enter the Red Zone.

Meanwhile, Rafiq Nizamani, the vice president of the teachers’ association, told Dawn that in 2021, the Sindh government had chalked out an “education policy” under which it was decided that teachers would not be promoted and they would remain in the same pay scale.

He said they launched a protest against this “arbitrary” decision as others were being promoted, but not them. He said that at the time, the government had assured them that their demands would be addressed, but this did not happen.

He said apart from the service structure, their other demands pertained to delegating the powers of posting primary teachers to district government officials. He said that they wanted recruitment and the transfer/posting of teachers to be delegated to district officials.

According to Nizamani, as the protesters moved from KPC towards CM House, police resorted to tear gas and a baton charge.

He claimed that two teachers were also injured. Nizamani said that they had decided to set up a protest camp outside the KPC for the fulfilment of their demands.

He admitted that the education officials had approached them for talks, but said they considered it “delaying tactics” in view of their past unfulfilled promises and decided to hold a protest march.

KARACHI: Thirty-eight people were released after brief detention on Wednesday as police used tear gas and batons against protesting teachers headed towards Chief Minister House from Karachi Press Club (KPC).

Hundreds of teachers had gathered outside the press club at the call of the All Sindh Primary Teachers Association (ASPTA). They were headed towards CM House to present their demands that pertained to the service structure and called for delegating powers for transfers and postings to district officers.

The protesters chanted slogans and attempted to move towards the CM House. However, when they arrived near Fawara Chowk, police baton-charged them and used tear gas shells to push them back toward the press club.

Adjoining roads near the KPC were closed to traffic, according to a traffic police spokesperson.

South Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Syed Asad Raza told Dawn that all detained teachers “have been released at night”, after he confirmed in earlier comments that 38 people were taken into custody.

Speaking to Dawn earlier in the day, the DIG noted that a teachers’ organisation had announced a protest at the KPC, with a march planned toward the CM House.

He said prior to the protest, the administration made concerted efforts to resolve the matter through negotiations and engaged officials from the education department to facilitate meaningful dialogue.

The official said the protest leadership was categorically told that entry into the Red Zone — a term used to denote the area surrounding Governor House and Chief Minister House — would not be permitted. Nevertheless, the administration was directed to exhaust all available resources and make every effort to ensure a peaceful resolution through dialogue, he said.

Raza alleged that around 3:15pm, the protesters turned “violent, abandoned the course of negotiations and forcibly started advancing towards the CM House.”

He claimed that the protesting teachers “breached police barricades and resorted to pelting police personnel with stones, causing injuries to one official.”

“Upon reaching and crossing Kabir Masjid on Governor House Road, the situation escalated, compelling police to resort to shelling to disperse the violent mob and restore order,” said the South police chief.

He said during the operation, 38 protesters, including ASPTA President Ghulam Rasool Mahar and General Secretary Aijaz Ali Chandio, were taken into custody.

Raza insisted that police took drastic action as the teachers tried to enter the Red Zone.

Meanwhile, Rafiq Nizamani, the vice president of the teachers’ association, told Dawn that in 2021, the Sindh government had chalked out an “education policy” under which it was decided that teachers would not be promoted and they would remain in the same pay scale.

He said they launched a protest against this “arbitrary” decision as others were being promoted, but not them. He said that at the time, the government had assured them that their demands would be addressed, but this did not happen.

He said apart from the service structure, their other demands pertained to delegating the powers of posting primary teachers to district government officials. He said that they wanted recruitment and the transfer/posting of teachers to be delegated to district officials.

According to Nizamani, as the protesters moved from KPC towards CM House, police resorted to tear gas and a baton charge.

He claimed that two teachers were also injured. Nizamani said that they had decided to set up a protest camp outside the KPC for the fulfilment of their demands.

He admitted that the education officials had approached them for talks, but said they considered it “delaying tactics” in view of their past unfulfilled promises and decided to hold a protest march.

headline: US Vice President JD Vance says Iran war is 'the reason we lost' midterms
description: Vance, a longtime vocal critic of US foreign interventionism, has reportedly been sceptical behind the scenes about the war on Iran.
author: AFP
article_text:
US Vice President JD Vance said on Wednesday that the Iran war had doomed Republicans in the midterm elections, moving to distance himself from the unpopular conflict ahead of a possible 2028 White House run.

“The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night,” Vance said in a lengthy post on X — apparently referring to President Donald Trump’s remarks that the Iran war was “part of it” but that it was still justified.

“If you’d like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that’s at least honest,” added Vance.

“But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there.”

The Democratic wave in Tuesday’s midterms has raised major questions over Vance’s previous status as the frontrunner for the Republican nomination in the 2028 presidential election. He has not yet formally declared that he will run.

Vance, a longtime vocal critic of US foreign interventionism, had reportedly been sceptical behind the scenes about the war on Iran that Trump and Israel launched in late February.

Vance also acknowledged that Republican voters who backed Trump and himself two years ago had switched sides due to the war and its effects on the US economy.

“The main problem is that many people who voted for Trump/Vance in 2024 voted for Democrats in 2026,” the vice president said.

He said a pollster that he respected showed that the Iran war and the economy were key factors in voters abandoning Republicans.

“In his polling, he saw that a lot of Trump 2024 voters were angry and planning to vote for Democrats,” Vance wrote. “He asked those voters who had abandoned us what would cause them to come back on our team. The top four answers, accounting for nearly all of the responses, were:

End the war
Focus on cost of living/inflation
Put America First
Change our relationship to Israel.”

Top Senate Democrat says Iran war ‘must end’

Meanwhile, Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer said that the Iran war “must end” and suggested his party’s incoming majority in Congress could use their control over government funding to press for that goal.

“The American people don’t know what the heck we’re fighting for in Iran,” Schumer tells journalists, adding that Trump has never made it clear and “changes his mind day to day, minute to minute”.

“This war must end. It must end,” Schumer added.

He later noted that the “power of the purse” is “one of the ways of deterring a president who does war without the consent of the American people”.

“Make no mistake: whenever Trump defies the will of the American people or the law, we will launch investigations, take him to court and entangle him in legislative razor wire,” Schumer warns. “The days of Trump’s supplicant Senate are over.”

headline: Petrol price dropped by Rs7.06 per litre, high-speed diesel by Rs3.71
description: Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs362.00 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs387.81.
author: News Desk
article_text:
The government on Wednesday cut the price of petrol by Rs7.06 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.71.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs362.00 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs387.81 on Nov 5 (Thursday), according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

Wednesday’s cut is the third consecutive reduction in fuel prices.

It came as international oil prices fell under $100 in volatile trade on Wednesday, with investors awaiting Washington’s next move in the US-Israeli war with Iran after President Donald Trump’s Republican Party lost control of Congress in midterm elections.

Brent futures were down $4.50, or 4.3 per cent, to $99.07 a barrel at 1619 GMT (9:19pm, PKT), while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures are down $4.13, or 4.3pc, to $92.02.

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Monday for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

Addressing a press conference on Tuesday, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said efforts were being made to introduce a similar system for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

Meanwhile, the Jamaat-i-Islami and the government are set to follow up on their recent discussions on possible relief in petroleum prices and hold another round of talks on Thursday, the party said.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

On Sept 13, PM Shehbaz also announced a “relief scheme” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, the petroleum minister announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

Additional input by Reuters

article_html:
The government on Wednesday cut the price of petrol by Rs7.06 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.71.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs362.00 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs387.81 on Nov 5 (Thursday), according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

Wednesday’s cut is the third consecutive reduction in fuel prices.

It came as international oil prices fell under $100 in volatile trade on Wednesday, with investors awaiting Washington’s next move in the US-Israeli war with Iran after President Donald Trump’s Republican Party lost control of Congress in midterm elections.

Brent futures were down $4.50, or 4.3 per cent, to $99.07 a barrel at 1619 GMT (9:19pm, PKT), while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures are down $4.13, or 4.3pc, to $92.02.

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Monday for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

Addressing a press conference on Tuesday, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said efforts were being made to introduce a similar system for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

Meanwhile, the Jamaat-i-Islami and the government are set to follow up on their recent discussions on possible relief in petroleum prices and hold another round of talks on Thursday, the party said.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

On Sept 13, PM Shehbaz also announced a “relief scheme” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, the petroleum minister announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

Additional input by Reuters

headline: Big money flops as Democrats sweep US Congress
description: “Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn’t work this time,” Elon Musk says after contributing nearly half a billion dollars to Republican efforts.
author: AFP
article_text:
Hundreds of millions of dollars spent, with little to show for it.

The rout of President Donald Trump and his Republicans in the US midterm elections was also a defeat for Elon Musk and for the massive campaign spending meant to sway voters.

Democrats captured both the Senate and House of Representatives on Tuesday in a stunning rejection of Trump’s political agenda, winning races in which conservative groups had poured in far more outside money than their liberal counterparts.

“This might have been the biggest defeat for big money in American political history,” Logan Phillips, founder of the election forecasting site Race to the White House, wrote on X.

“Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn’t work this time,” Musk said on X, with a shrug emoji.

Musk contributed nearly half a billion dollars to Republican efforts, making him the largest individual contributor in a federal election cycle since 2010, according to campaign finance tracker OpenSecrets.

That year, the Supreme Court ruled that the government cannot limit political spending by corporations, unions and other groups acting independently of candidates, opening the way for big donors to pour vast sums into elections, sometimes anonymously.

‘Our own Goliaths’

More than $200 million of Musk’s money went to support Ken Paxton, the Republican Senate candidate in Texas.

Democrat James Talarico defeated Paxton, a close Trump ally, to become the first Democrat to win statewide office in Texas since 1994.

“In this race, we went up against our own Goliaths. The richest man in the world, the most powerful man in the world and the entire Washington, DC establishment,” Talarico said.

He also targeted billionaires “who own the social media algorithms, who own the cable news networks, who own the politicians fighting on our screens” and who “want us at each other’s throats”.

In Ohio, Democrat Sherrod Brown unseated Republican Senator Jon Husted in the country’s second most expensive race, with more than $500m spent.

In Georgia, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms defeated billionaire health care executive Rick Jackson in the governor’s race, after he poured more than $200m of his fortune into his bid, according to the Atlanta Journal-Constitution.

In Ohio, biotech billionaire Vivek Ramaswamy lost the governor’s race to Democrat Amy Acton after putting an estimated $36m of his own money into it.

AI industry money also fell short.

In South Carolina, American Mission, the Republican arm of the Leading the Future network backed by OpenAI president Greg Brockman and venture firm Andreessen Horowitz, put about $2.7m behind Senator Darline Graham, who lost to Democrat Annie Andrews in a state Trump won by 18 points.

Building the Future, a new data centre industry super PAC tied to Leading the Future, had made Graham its first candidate to back.

‘Cannot yield’

Democrats also had billionaire backing. Former New York mayor Michael Bloomberg spent $80m on House, Senate and governor races, then added $36m in the final days, Politico reported.

Bloomberg’s political adviser Howard Wolfson told CNN that “money is not determinative, but it is helpful”, noting that Republicans held a significant financial advantage.

LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman, who put $11.5m into the super PAC backing Talarico, said “we should get money out of politics”.

“And while people like Elon are spending outrageous amounts to keep authoritarian clowns in power, those of us who believe in the ideals of America cannot yield,” Hoffman wrote on X late on Tuesday, defending his largesse.

In California, a ballot proposal for a one-time five per cent tax on the state’s billionaires seemed to have failed after some of its wealthiest residents spent hundreds of millions of dollars to defeat it.

“Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn’t work this time,” Musk said on X, with a shrug emoji.

Musk contributed nearly half a billion dollars to Republican efforts, making him the largest individual contributor in a federal election cycle since 2010, according to campaign finance tracker OpenSecrets.

That year, the Supreme Court ruled that the government cannot limit political spending by corporations, unions and other groups acting independently of candidates, opening the way for big donors to pour vast sums into elections, sometimes anonymously.
