More than $200 million of Musk’s money went to support Ken Paxton, the Republican Senate candidate in Texas.

Democrat James Talarico defeated Paxton, a close Trump ally, to become the first Democrat to win statewide office in Texas since 1994.

“In this race, we went up against our own Goliaths. The richest man in the world, the most powerful man in the world and the entire Washington, DC establishment,” Talarico said.

He also targeted billionaires “who own the social media algorithms, who own the cable news networks, who own the politicians fighting on our screens” and who “want us at each other’s throats”.

In Ohio, Democrat Sherrod Brown unseated Republican Senator Jon Husted in the country’s second most expensive race, with more than $500m spent.

In Georgia, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms defeated billionaire health care executive Rick Jackson in the governor’s race, after he poured more than $200m of his fortune into his bid, according to the Atlanta Journal-Constitution.

In Ohio, biotech billionaire Vivek Ramaswamy lost the governor’s race to Democrat Amy Acton after putting an estimated $36m of his own money into it.

AI industry money also fell short.

In South Carolina, American Mission, the Republican arm of the Leading the Future network backed by OpenAI president Greg Brockman and venture firm Andreessen Horowitz, put about $2.7m behind Senator Darline Graham, who lost to Democrat Annie Andrews in a state Trump won by 18 points.

Building the Future, a new data centre industry super PAC tied to Leading the Future, had made Graham its first candidate to back.

‘Cannot yield’

Democrats also had billionaire backing. Former New York mayor Michael Bloomberg spent $80m on House, Senate and governor races, then added $36m in the final days, Politico reported.

Bloomberg’s political adviser Howard Wolfson told CNN that “money is not determinative, but it is helpful”, noting that Republicans held a significant financial advantage.

LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman, who put $11.5m into the super PAC backing Talarico, said “we should get money out of politics”.

“And while people like Elon are spending outrageous amounts to keep authoritarian clowns in power, those of us who believe in the ideals of America cannot yield,” Hoffman wrote on X late on Tuesday, defending his largesse.

In California, a ballot proposal for a one-time five per cent tax on the state’s billionaires seemed to have failed after some of its wealthiest residents spent hundreds of millions of dollars to defeat it.

headline: Seeing red in Iran
description: The US today faces its own Great Game fallout.
author: Mahir Ali
article_text:
IN the run-up to yesterday’s US mid-term elections, it became obvious that, almost four decades after the Cold War ended, the ‘spectre of communism’ Marx and Engels identified in the 19th century still haunts Western consciousness.

Islamophobia might have been the most prominent weapon, but it was accompanied by diatribes against Marxists and communists, invariably directed against people who are neither. For good measure, some of them are simultaneously derided as Islamist jihadists.

The American establishment’s obsession with the communist threat, real or imagined, dates back to the early 20th century, and has served as a guiding principle of its foreign (and domestic) policy since the Truman era.

One of the CIA’s first interventions, against Iranian democracy in the early 1950s, was justified as a blow against communist influence, even though the popular nationalist Mohammad Mossadegh was barely left of centre. Furthermore, the communist party Tudeh had initially misidentified him as a mole for US interests, recognising only belatedly that his oil nationalisation was in Iran’s interest.

The party was decimated in the wake of the CIA-guided coup that re-established the Shah’s reign, under the aegis of Savak, MI6, and Mossad. The survivors fled abroad, mostly ending up in East Germany, although many underground operatives remained in situ, and retained some influence in the military arm of the state.

Thus, when Tudeh resurfaced in the lead-up to the 1979 revolution, it wasn’t starting from scratch. It participated in the mass surge against the tyrannical Shah, but, unlike the militant Mujahideen-i-Khalq and others on the left, acknowledged the Khomeini phenomenon as a legitimate expression of the popular will.

That helps to explain why Tudeh briefly became the main opposition in a milieu dominated by the Islamic Republican Party. It’s unlikely this arrangement would anyhow have lasted long, but things came to a head in 1982-83.

The US today faces its own Great Game fallout.

The saga is laid out in entertaining detail in espionage specialist author Ben Macin­t­yre’s recently published Redwood — a fascinating, albeit somewhat breathless, account of the defection in Tehran of a senior KGB officer, Vladimir Kuzichkin, the Soviet point man for contacts with Tudeh and a network of spies.

In Macintyre’s reading, Kuzichkin was disillusioned with his corrupt colleagues, as well as with the Soviet polity, but above all, it was his impotence that drove him to risk approaching MI6, expecting Western medicine to offer a cure. (Viagra was more than a decade away, but MI6 was able to organise a discreet circumcision.)

More significantly, Kuzichkin passed on to MI6’s Ian McCredie his list of Iranian contacts and details of communications with Moscow. MI6 shared them with the CIA, which was unable to operate in Iran at the time, and the latter insisted on sharing them with Iran’s intelligence agencies.

Iran had only recently released the hostages taken at the US embassy, but while the American cold warriors might not have been fans of the clergy, in their blinkered worldview the communist threat was paramount. MI6 was happy, as always, to play second fiddle. The suspicion was that Moscow’s arms and gold were preparing Tudeh for a coup that could pave the way for a Soviet invasion, as in Afghanistan, and further tilt the Cold War imbalance towards communism.

By 1982, it should have been obvious to Moscow that the Afghan occupation was going awry — thanks largely to the CIA’s covert war via Pakistan. Macintyre does not mention Zbigniew Brzezinski’s role, through the CIA and regional assets, in luring the Red Army into its biggest folly. But, giv­en the state of aff­airs in the nei­­ghbourhood, it’s unl­ikely Moscow wou­ld seriously have contemplated a sim­ilar misadventure in Iran.

Non­etheless, it was decided to impart Redwood’s information to the Iranian authorities, and the chosen venue was Islamabad, courtesy of the then ISI chief Gen Abdul Rehman Akhtar.

Even though senior elements of the Iranian leadership — including Ayatollah Khomeini, parliamentary speaker Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, and prime minister Mir-Hossein Mousavi — had their doubts about the imminence of a communist coup attempt and advised restraint, the president Ali Khamenei and Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps chief Mohsen Rezaei favoured haste, leading to thousands of arrests and mass executions, alongside torture and televised ‘confessions’.

As in Afghanistan earlier this century, the US is today confronted, in part, with the consequences of its own Great Game machinations. But ask any surviving cold warrior, and most likely they’ll still contend it was a price worth paying for keeping the world safe from communism.

Many of us, meanwhile, awaiting this week’s election results, look forward to the impending demise of the American empire.

headline: Trump says Iran war has been worth it despite election losses
description: US President Donald Trump says the Iran war has been worthwhile despite acknowledging its role in losses in US...
article_text:

US President Donald Trump has acknowledged that the Iran war was the key factor in his party’s sweeping midterm election losses, after Vice President JD Vance urged Republicans to be “honest” about the unpopular conflict’s impact, AFP reports.

Asked if he agreed with Vance’s remark that the way was “the reason we lost,” Trump, speaking to reporters at his White House ballroom construction site, says: “I think it’s largely true because it drove the gasoline up a little bit short term. But at the same time, if I had it to do again, I’d have to do it again. Because long term, it’s the only answer. You can’t let Iran have a nuclear weapon.”

headline: US sanctions Indian companies over alleged maritime fraud aiding Iranian vessels
description: US Treasury claims network aided Iranian vessels in sailing under false flags and in gaining fake maritime certifications.
author: AFP
article_text:
The United States on Wednesday issued sanctions targeting what it described as a “vast criminal network” run by two Indian nationals that was aiding Iran’s shadow fleet of oil tankers in committing maritime fraud.

In a statement, the US Treasury said the network aided Iranian vessels in sailing under false flags and in gaining fake maritime certifications.

The move was the latest in a tightening web of US sanctions targeting Iran since August, when Washington announced that it would be seeking the “economic asphyxiation” of the country in conjunction with its military campaign.

The United States and Israel launched a war against Iran in late February, plunging the Middle East into violence as Tehran’s retaliatory action struck US allies and closed a vital energy trade waterway.

“As we have said many times, under Operation Economic Outcast, you are either with us or against us,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who has in the past threatened sanctions against any country or company that aids Iran, regardless of its relationship with Washington.

“We know where you are, and we will sanction those who continue supporting the Iranian regime, whether by land, sea, or air.”

Wednesday’s sanctions named Indian nationals Suniel Kumar Sharma and his wife Jaspreet Preeti Shahid as operating a large-scale maritime fraud network from their base in Chandigarh.

“Purporting to represent nations from nearly every continent, from Guyana to Eswatini and Laos, Sharma and Shahid have allowed the Iranian shadow fleet… to evade international restrictions on their operation,” the Treasury said in a statement.

The sanctions also targeted two other Indian nationals and a number of companies Treasury said were part of the network.

Wednesday’s action also saw Washington sanction Turkiye-based Fugo Ground Services Inc for allegedly continuing to provide services to Iran’s aviation sector, which the United States has sought to shut down.

Earlier this month, the United States imposed sanctions targeting “the remnants of Iran’s shadow fleet” of tankers used to transport oil products to foreign markets, affecting 17 vessels.

headline: 'United opposition' gathers at Fazl's Islamabad residence, vows stronger alliance
description: Meeting comprising key TTAP, PTI and JUI-F leaders decides to form committees to resolve differences; PTI alarmed over Imran’s reportedly high blood pressure.
author: Kalbe Ali, Ikram Junaidi, News Desk
article_text:
Opposition leaders on Wednesday gathered at the residence of Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman in Islamabad and agreed to strengthen their alliance and parliamentary coordination.

After a meeting during which they discussed several matters, including the emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, JUI-F and TTAP decided to form committees to resolve mutual differences and take forward consultations on a multi-party conference (MPC).

National Assembly (NA) and Senate opposition leaders, Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, respectively, attended the meeting. MNA Asad Qaiser, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, NA Chief Whip Amir Dogar and Senator Noorul Haq Qadri were present from PTI.

Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) — headed by Achakzai — termed it a meeting of a “united opposition”.

An earlier statement by JUI-F said the gathering was to discuss “the situation of emergency and governor’s rule” in KP, as well as plans for an MPC.

In its statement, TTAP said the meeting was also “discussing unity and solidarity among opposition parties, the supremacy of the Constitution and law, the protection of democratic rights, a joint strategy to address the current political situation, and a future course of action”.

On Aug 20, following a meeting between Fazl and Achakzai, the alliance and JUI-F had announced plans to form a “united opposition”.

Speaking to the media after the meeting, Achakzai said the delegation had called on Fazl with the objective of building an alliance to strengthen Parliament.

He condemned what he described as a character assassination campaign against the JUI-F chief and declared that the opposition stood firmly with him.

He added that the possibility of convening an MPC was also discussed during the meeting.

In his remarks, Fazl also said the opposition would work to strengthen its presence in Parliament and protect the interests of every part of the country.

Referring to the former Federally Administered Tribal Areas (Fata), he said his party had opposed the 2018 merger, adding that the issue was now being linked to a struggle over resources.

He also expressed concern over what he alleged were attempts to bring Gwadar, the coastal belt and Sindh’s islands under federal control.

The JUI-F chief said the opposition had already represented the people’s concerns regarding the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP, stressing that it was speaking about the public mandate and national interests.

The leaders agreed to continue consultations and establish a committee to address differences among opposition parties.

Senator Abbas alleged that the governor’s rule had been illegally imposed in KP and accused the authorities of targeting those who raised their voices for the country’s welfare.

On its part, the Centre maintains that the security situation in the province and the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the counterterrorism fight “compelled” it to take the measures on Oct 11.

Addressing reporters, the Senate opposition leader lamented that the sanctity of homes and the privacy of citizens were being violated as authorities detained people from their residences.

He warned of decreasing public confidence in the country’s institutions, claiming Pakistan had reached one of the worst periods in its history.

TTAP said its spokesperson Akhundzada Hussain Ahmad Yousafzai, PTI founder Imran Khan’s legal counsel Khalid Yousaf Chaudhry, and Agha Nasir Shirazi also attended the meeting.

The JUI-F team included its vice-president and KP chapter president Senator Maulana Attaur Rehman, senators Kamran Murtaza and Maulana Attaul Haq Darwish, alongside party members Akram Khan Durrani, Aslam Ghauri, Maulana Salahuddin Ayubi, Hafiz Hamdullah and Zahid Durrani.

PTI alarmed over Imran’s ‘high blood pressure’

Meanwhile, PTI’s Raja raised concerns about Imran’s health, saying his blood pressure was not under control. He thanked Fazl for supporting the PTI and alleged that the JUI-F chief was being “punished” for standing with the party.

Imran — in prison since Aug 5, 2023 in multiple cases — had complained of uncontrolled and fluctuating blood pressure along with palpitations, headache and restlessness in early August, according to annexures attached to a jail report submitted to the Supreme Court (SC).

In an official statement issued today, PTI expressed grave concern over its founder’s health, saying his blood pressure had surged to 192. It demanded his immediate transfer to Shifa International Hospital for independent medical treatment under the supervision of his personal physicians.

PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram said repeated fluctuations in the ex-cricketer’s blood pressure were a matter of extreme concern, stressing that protecting his health was the responsibility of the state.

He accused the government of denying Imran adequate medical facilities, family access and treatment of his choice.

He demanded immediate implementation of the SC’s Aug 18 order directing Imran’s transfer to Shifa International Hospital, with treatment supervised by his personal and family-appointed doctors.

Imran’s eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) — came to light in late January. While he has undergone eye procedures and check-ups at the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims), his family demands that he be shifted to a hospital of his choice.

The government and the opposition have been engaged in a blame game, with the latter accusing the former of a lack of transparency on the matter, of not ensuring appropriate treatment for Imran, and of not allowing his personal physicians access to him.

The government denies these allegations, saying the required medical treatment is being ensured and ample facilities are being provided at the Adiala jail, including a healthy diet plan and exercise equipment.

Fazl’s PTI ties amid row with Centre

Wednesday’s gathering came a day after PTI said it would welcome support from Fazl in its struggle against the government, with Raja telling the media that the party would welcome anyone who stood by it and supported its struggle.

“It is possible that some may walk with us for one mile, some for 10 miles, and some may go with us till the end. But why should we reject them?” the PTI secretary general said.

Fazl has been critical of the federal government over the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. He accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments amid his efforts to mediate between the federal and KP governments.

Since mid-October, the veteran politician and key federal ministers have also made harsh remarks against each other, after Fazl accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights.

Last week, Fazl accused the government of misusing the Constitution and resorting to unconstitutional measures in imposing the emergency.

In September, TTAP and PTI leaders said they intended to hold consultations to call an MPC to discuss several issues, including the creation of new provinces, law and order, and the economy. This was prior to the government’s declaration of emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11.

In the days preceding the emergency, political tensions between the Centre and the opposition — including the PTI, which was in power in KP — had remained high since Imran’s party announced a protest march to Islamabad to demand his release.

article_html:
Opposition leaders on Wednesday gathered at the residence of Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman in Islamabad and agreed to strengthen their alliance and parliamentary coordination.

After a meeting during which they discussed several matters, including the emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, JUI-F and TTAP decided to form committees to resolve mutual differences and take forward consultations on a multi-party conference (MPC).

National Assembly (NA) and Senate opposition leaders, Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, respectively, attended the meeting. MNA Asad Qaiser, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, NA Chief Whip Amir Dogar and Senator Noorul Haq Qadri were present from PTI.

Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) — headed by Achakzai — termed it a meeting of a “united opposition”.

An earlier statement by JUI-F said the gathering was to discuss “the situation of emergency and governor’s rule” in KP, as well as plans for an MPC.

In its statement, TTAP said the meeting was also “discussing unity and solidarity among opposition parties, the supremacy of the Constitution and law, the protection of democratic rights, a joint strategy to address the current political situation, and a future course of action”.

On Aug 20, following a meeting between Fazl and Achakzai, the alliance and JUI-F had announced plans to form a “united opposition”.

Speaking to the media after the meeting, Achakzai said the delegation had called on Fazl with the objective of building an alliance to strengthen Parliament.

He condemned what he described as a character assassination campaign against the JUI-F chief and declared that the opposition stood firmly with him.

He added that the possibility of convening an MPC was also discussed during the meeting.

In his remarks, Fazl also said the opposition would work to strengthen its presence in Parliament and protect the interests of every part of the country.

Referring to the former Federally Administered Tribal Areas (Fata), he said his party had opposed the 2018 merger, adding that the issue was now being linked to a struggle over resources.

He also expressed concern over what he alleged were attempts to bring Gwadar, the coastal belt and Sindh’s islands under federal control.

The JUI-F chief said the opposition had already represented the people’s concerns regarding the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP, stressing that it was speaking about the public mandate and national interests.

The leaders agreed to continue consultations and establish a committee to address differences among opposition parties.

Senator Abbas alleged that the governor’s rule had been illegally imposed in KP and accused the authorities of targeting those who raised their voices for the country’s welfare.

On its part, the Centre maintains that the security situation in the province and the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the counterterrorism fight “compelled” it to take the measures on Oct 11.

Addressing reporters, the Senate opposition leader lamented that the sanctity of homes and the privacy of citizens were being violated as authorities detained people from their residences.

He warned of decreasing public confidence in the country’s institutions, claiming Pakistan had reached one of the worst periods in its history.

TTAP said its spokesperson Akhundzada Hussain Ahmad Yousafzai, PTI founder Imran Khan’s legal counsel Khalid Yousaf Chaudhry, and Agha Nasir Shirazi also attended the meeting.

The JUI-F team included its vice-president and KP chapter president Senator Maulana Attaur Rehman, senators Kamran Murtaza and Maulana Attaul Haq Darwish, alongside party members Akram Khan Durrani, Aslam Ghauri, Maulana Salahuddin Ayubi, Hafiz Hamdullah and Zahid Durrani.

PTI alarmed over Imran’s ‘high blood pressure’

Meanwhile, PTI’s Raja raised concerns about Imran’s health, saying his blood pressure was not under control. He thanked Fazl for supporting the PTI and alleged that the JUI-F chief was being “punished” for standing with the party.

Imran — in prison since Aug 5, 2023 in multiple cases — had complained of uncontrolled and fluctuating blood pressure along with palpitations, headache and restlessness in early August, according to annexures attached to a jail report submitted to the Supreme Court (SC).

In an official statement issued today, PTI expressed grave concern over its founder’s health, saying his blood pressure had surged to 192. It demanded his immediate transfer to Shifa International Hospital for independent medical treatment under the supervision of his personal physicians.

PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram said repeated fluctuations in the ex-cricketer’s blood pressure were a matter of extreme concern, stressing that protecting his health was the responsibility of the state.

He accused the government of denying Imran adequate medical facilities, family access and treatment of his choice.

He demanded immediate implementation of the SC’s Aug 18 order directing Imran’s transfer to Shifa International Hospital, with treatment supervised by his personal and family-appointed doctors.

Imran’s eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) — came to light in late January. While he has undergone eye procedures and check-ups at the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims), his family demands that he be shifted to a hospital of his choice.

The government and the opposition have been engaged in a blame game, with the latter accusing the former of a lack of transparency on the matter, of not ensuring appropriate treatment for Imran, and of not allowing his personal physicians access to him.

The government denies these allegations, saying the required medical treatment is being ensured and ample facilities are being provided at the Adiala jail, including a healthy diet plan and exercise equipment.

Fazl’s PTI ties amid row with Centre

Wednesday’s gathering came a day after PTI said it would welcome support from Fazl in its struggle against the government, with Raja telling the media that the party would welcome anyone who stood by it and supported its struggle.

“It is possible that some may walk with us for one mile, some for 10 miles, and some may go with us till the end. But why should we reject them?” the PTI secretary general said.

Fazl has been critical of the federal government over the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. He accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments amid his efforts to mediate between the federal and KP governments.

Since mid-October, the veteran politician and key federal ministers have also made harsh remarks against each other, after Fazl accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights.

Last week, Fazl accused the government of misusing the Constitution and resorting to unconstitutional measures in imposing the emergency.

In September, TTAP and PTI leaders said they intended to hold consultations to call an MPC to discuss several issues, including the creation of new provinces, law and order, and the economy. This was prior to the government’s declaration of emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11.

In the days preceding the emergency, political tensions between the Centre and the opposition — including the PTI, which was in power in KP — had remained high since Imran’s party announced a protest march to Islamabad to demand his release.

“It is possible that some may walk with us for one mile, some for 10 miles, and some may go with us till the end. But why should we reject them?” the PTI secretary general said.

Fazl has been critical of the federal government over the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. He accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments amid his efforts to mediate between the federal and KP governments.
Since mid-October, the veteran politician and key federal ministers have also made harsh remarks against each other, after Fazl accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights.
Last week, Fazl accused the government of misusing the Constitution and resorting to unconstitutional measures in imposing the emergency.

In September, TTAP and PTI leaders said they intended to hold consultations to call an MPC to discuss several issues, including the creation of new provinces, law and order, and the economy. This was prior to the government’s declaration of emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11.

In the days preceding the emergency, political tensions between the Centre and the opposition — including the PTI, which was in power in KP — had remained high since Imran’s party announced a protest march to Islamabad to demand his release.
